back: The chance that a threat exploits a vulnerability, together with the harm that would result: judged by likelihood and impact.
Avoid (remove the cause), reduce (lower likelihood or impact), transfer (pass the financial loss on, e.g. insurance), accept (live with a small risk).
Score = likelihood × impact (each 1 to 5). Low 1-5, Medium 6-12, High 15-25 in this course.
A documented plan to restore systems and data after a failure: backups, off-site copies, alternative site, tested restore and named roles.
Full copies everything; incremental copies only what changed since the last backup, using less time and storage. Restore needs the last full plus the incrementals.
Hot: equipped and up to date, fastest and dearest. Warm: equipment but data to restore. Cold: space and power only, slowest and cheapest.
Acceptable use, access control, data handling, backup and recovery, incident response, training and discipline.
A backup that has never been restored may not work; plans are tested regularly.
